column1: # Every QA gate scripts/qa-all.bash runs, in the order it runs them. Tab separated; # starts a
# comment line. The order is part of the contract: the stage lines come out in this order and a
# failure never stops the gates after it. src-go/qa/gates loads this file strictly (a short row,
# an unknown kind or reader, a bad name or pattern, a duplicate, or a missing script is exit 2
# with the line number); qa-changed reads its suite population from it and the QA.md inventory
# gate (src-go/qa/docs) checks the documentation against it. SPEC-qa-all.md section 11.
#   kind     gate     run, capture stdout+stderr, status 0 passes; the readers give the summary
#            stage    one of the seven jq-merged report stages: run with QA_JSON_OUT, output
#                     streamed live, status 2 aborts the whole run with the text as its message
#            drift    like gate, but its own output is the stage line (no summary to read)
#            helpers  the helper unit suite: counts travel in a file, not in text
#   name     the stage-line name, [a-z0-9-]+ (helpers/qa_environment/verdicts.py parses it)
#   command  words relative to the repository root; scripts/x.bash runs through bash
#   text     gate/drift/helpers: the reason on the failed stage line; stage: the exit-2 message
#   reader   gate rows, one or more, joined with "; " on the pass line:
#              count          the last "passed: N" the suite printed
#              detail:<ERE>   the text the POSIX ERE matches on the last line that matches
#            A gate whose reader finds nothing FAILS: it proved nothing.
# Adding a gate is adding a row here (and a row in CLAUDE/QA.md). Nothing else lists the gates.
# Toolchain first: every verdict below is a property of the binary that produced it. It does
# not abort, because a drifted toolchain makes the verdicts unreliable, not unrunnable.
